app.title: Lactomeda — Mission Control
app.tagline: Design a space mission, then keep it alive.

scenario.heading: Choose your mission
scenario.intro: Every scenario has its own goal, budget and deadline. There is no single right design — pick one and start planning.

placeholder.hint: Walk with WASD, press E at a station.

requirements.heading: Set your targets
requirements.intro: Turn the goals of {{name}} into numbers you will be judged on. Harder targets can earn more points, but they make the spacecraft harder to design.

levelHelp.threshold: The minimum. Below this, the objective fails.
levelHelp.baseline: What the mission promises. A solid, balanced choice.
levelHelp.goal: The stretch target. Best science, hardest design.

requirements.potentialHelp: Average of your levels. Applied to the objectives part of the final score.
requirements.pressureNone: Nothing above baseline — a balanced start.

payload.heading: Pick your instruments
payload.intro: Instruments collect the science. Each one adds mass, power, cost and data that the rest of the spacecraft must carry.
payload.noBus: No bus chosen yet: instrument slot limits will apply once you pick a spacecraft size.
payload.slotsFull: No free instrument slot on this bus. Remove one or choose a bigger bus.
payload.helpsNone: Not used by this mission’s objectives

incompatible.objective: Measures nothing this mission needs. Mission goals: {{needs}}.
incompatible.orbit: Only works from {{orbits}}, and this mission can’t fly there.
incompatible.chosenOrbit: Doesn’t work from your chosen orbit ({{orbit}}).
incompatible.title: Not available

payload.marginal_one: +{{value}} science, half because you already have one

orbit.heading: Choose your orbit
orbit.intro: Where your spacecraft flies decides how sharp its images are, how long it sits in shadow, how often it can talk to the ground and how harsh the radiation is.
orbit.notAllowed: This mission can’t fly here: it is outside the scenario’s allowed orbits.
orbit.instrumentsLost: Your instruments that won’t work here: {{names}}

leo.goodFor: Sharp Earth images and low-cost missions close to home.
leo.tradeoff: Short ground contacts, and air drag slowly pulls the spacecraft down.

sso.goodFor: Earth observation with the same lighting every day.
sso.tradeoff: Needs more launch energy than a plain low orbit.

meo.tradeoff: Strong radiation from the Van Allen belts.

geo.goodFor: Weather and nonstop watch over one region.
geo.tradeoff: Low image detail, expensive launch and a long way to talk to.

molniya.goodFor: Long views of the far north.
molniya.tradeoff: Crosses the radiation belts twice a day.

l2.goodFor: Telescopes: stable, cold, with the Sun always behind.
l2.tradeoff: Needs the Deep Space Network, and data comes down slowly.

lunar.tradeoff: Takes a lot of fuel to get there, and comms are far away.

mars.goodFor: Mars science and relaying rover data.
mars.tradeoff: Sunlight is only 43% of Earth’s, and the trip takes months.

orbit.confirmNeeds: Pick an orbit, a launcher and ground stations to continue.

launcher.heading: Choose your launcher
launcher.intro: The rocket must lift your spacecraft to the orbit you chose. Bigger rockets carry more and reach farther, but cost more. Cheaper rides can be less reliable.
launcher.pickOrbitFirst: Pick an orbit above to see which launchers can reach it.

ground.heading: Choose your ground stations
ground.intro: Your spacecraft can only send data home while a ground station can see it. More and bigger stations give more minutes of contact per day, but cost more every year.
ground.pickOrbit: Pick an orbit to see the minutes
ground.tooFar: Too far: reaches up to {{reach}}, your orbit is {{distance}} away.

catalog.gn-university: One small dish on campus. Cheap, but it only sees you for a few passes a day.
catalog.gn-commercial: A rented network of stations around the world: many more passes per day.
catalog.gn-nen: NASA’s network for spacecraft near Earth, out to the Moon and L2.
catalog.gn-dsn: NASA’s giant dishes in California, Spain and Australia. The only way to talk to deep space.

cml.heading: Concept maturity (JPL CML)
cml.debriefNone: Your concept has not reached CML 1 yet.
cml.help: NASA JPL rates how mature a mission concept is with Concept Maturity Levels. Each phase of the game moves your concept up one level.

segments.heading: Mission segments
segments.help: NASA splits every science mission into four segments: launch, space, ground and user.
segments.summaryIntro: Your design so far, organised the way NASA plans a science mission.

users.student-cubesat: Your university team, space-weather researchers and radio amateurs who listen to your CubeSat.
users.wildfire-eo: Firefighters and emergency agencies, who use fresh fire maps to decide where to send crews.
users.space-telescope: Astronomers around the world, who request observing time and download the data from public archives.

bus.heading: Build your spacecraft
bus.intro: The bus is the spacecraft around your instruments: its frame, power, computer and radio. Bigger buses carry more, but cost more and need bigger rockets.
bus.partsHeading: 2. Pick one part for each subsystem
bus.trlHelp: Technology Readiness Level: 9 = flown many times, lower = newer and riskier.
bus.confirmNeeds: Choose a bus size and a part for every subsystem to continue.

structure.name: Structure
structure.what: The frame that holds everything together.

power.name: Power
power.what: Makes electricity: solar panels, or an RTG far from the Sun.

battery.name: Battery
battery.what: Keeps everything running while the spacecraft is in shadow.

computer.name: Computer
computer.what: Runs the spacecraft and stores data until it can be sent home.

attitude.name: Attitude control
attitude.what: Points the spacecraft: cameras at the target, antennas at Earth.

propulsion.name: Propulsion
propulsion.what: Thrusters to change orbit, dodge debris and stay up longer.

thermal.name: Thermal
thermal.what: Keeps parts not too hot and not too cold.

comms.name: Comms
comms.what: The radio that sends your data to the ground stations.

issues.UNKNOWN_COMPONENT: A part for {{subsystem}} no longer exists: pick another one.
issues.WRONG_SUBSYSTEM: That part does not belong to {{subsystem}}: pick another one.
issues.LOW_SOLAR_POWER: Far from the Sun, solar panels make much less power. Consider an RTG.
issues.TOO_MANY_INSTRUMENTS: Too many instruments for this bus: remove one or pick a bigger bus.
issues.TOO_MANY_COMPONENTS: Too many parts for this bus (backups count twice): pick a bigger bus.
issues.OVER_BUS_MASS: Too heavy for this bus: pick a bigger bus or lighter parts.
issues.UNKNOWN_BUS_CLASS: This bus size no longer exists: pick another one.

landing.subtitle: Mission Control
landing.tagline: Design a NASA-style space mission, then keep it alive.

hint.solo: Plan and fly a mission on your own.
hint.createRoom: Up to 4 players, each with a role.

landing.soonReason: Coming soon: this mode is still being built.

howTo.heading: How to play
howTo.design: Design: pick a mission, set its targets, then build the spacecraft, choose instruments, orbit, rocket and ground stations.
howTo.resources: Watch the resource bar: mass, power, budget, data, comms and time. Green is fine, amber is tight, red is over.
howTo.maturity: Every finished phase raises your concept maturity, like NASA JPL rates real mission ideas (CML 1 to 4).
howTo.flight: Fly: walk around your ship and answer emergencies at each station before time runs out.
howTo.debrief: Debrief: see your score and why the mission worked or failed, then fly again with one change.
